Expected results

  • Steps 4, 7 and 10: each drag opens the question "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" (with the example name: "Clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts?"). The line that is not approved ({Line-2}) and the declined line ({Line-4}) are ignored, and a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line counts.
  • Steps 5, 8 and 11: after Keep shifts each work order moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message names it: "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}", then "{Work-order-2} assigned to {Technician-B}" and "{Work-order-3} assigned to {Technician-B}", each with an Undo button.
  • Step 14: all three of {Technician-A}'s shifts are still on the Schedule tomorrow, at the same times.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R28 (reworded in version 49 from Chris Ward's answer 1 of 14 Oct 2026 to our question sheet: only approved lines count, judged when the lead changes), S4-R29, S4-R23 and S4-R5 (message wording changed in versions 66 and 68, 19 Oct 2026), read 19 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build. Re-read against PRD version 82 (29 Oct 2026) on 2 Nov 2026: the quoted rules are unchanged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R28: “The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line of the work order, judged at the moment the lead changes; this is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. Lines not yet approved, and declined lines, are ignored. On a work order with one line, a shift on that line counts, and so does a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line. A shift on only some approved lines does not show the prompt, and that includes an Entire work order shift once a line has been added and approved after it was made.”
  • S4-R29: “The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.”
  • S4-R23: “If the user chooses to keep shifts, change the lead technician and retain the existing shifts.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”

Last checked against build v26.43.5-77de68c (production) on 11/2/2026.
